Complete Empirical Research Plan: Air Quality and Housing Prices, 1970s–1990s, United States

----------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
----------------------------------------------------
Chosen method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) augmented with an event-study specification.

Rationale  
• The 1970 Clean Air Act (CAA) created sharp, plausibly exogenous changes in regulatory pressure that differed by county depending on whether the county was designated “non-attainment” for particulate matter (PM).  
• Counties did not self-select into non-attainment after 1971—the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) classified them based on pre-CAA ambient pollution relative to the new National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS).  
• Housing transactions can be linked to the county of location and thus inherit this quasi-experiment.  
• DID compares the evolution of housing prices in non-attainment (“treated”) versus attainment (“control”) counties before and after 1971.  
• An event-study extension (year-by-year treatment effects) permits pre-trend testing and dynamic effect tracing.

----------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
----------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Treated = 1 if the house is located in a county that was designated non-attainment for total suspended particulates (TSP, the PM metric used at the time) in the EPA’s first classification list (published December 1971).  
Treated = 0 for attainment counties (met the NAAQS for TSP).

Control group  
Attainment counties in the same state that were within the 25th–75th percentile of the pre-1970 TSP distribution (to avoid extremely clean or extremely dirty outliers). This limits compositional differences and absorbs state-level shocks through state-year fixed effects.

Treatment timing  
Post = 1 for transaction years ≥ 1972 (allowing one-year implementation lag), 0 for years 1965–1971.  
Event-study estimates will interact Treated with year dummies (1965 is omitted base year).

Running variable / cutoff  
Not applicable (method is DID, not RDD).

----------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
----------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel Trends: In the absence of the CAA, price trends in non-attainment and attainment counties would have evolved similarly.  
  • Plausibility: Counties on either side of the attainment cutoff had similar pre-1970 pollution but differed discretely in regulation once standards were set.  
  • Test: Plot event-study coefficients for years −6 to −1; they should be statistically indistinguishable from zero.

A2. No Differential Time-Varying Confounders: Other shocks (e.g., de-industrialization, recessions) do not differentially hit non-attainment counties conditional on controls & fixed effects.  
  • Plausibility: We control for county-specific linear trends, state-year fixed effects, and local labor-market covariates (employment, income).

A3. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA): Housing prices in one county do not respond to regulation status in another county (no spillovers).  
  • Plausibility: Inter-county migration could spill over, but within-state FE and a robustness drop of adjacent attainment counties mitigate this.

A4. Common Support: There exist houses both before and after 1971 in treated and control counties.

----------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Remedies
----------------------------------------------------
T1. Differential economic shocks (plant closures, oil crisis effects)  
  Remedy: Include county-industry employment shares interacted with year, county-specific linear (or quadratic) trends, and state-year fixed effects.

T2. Migration or compositional change (people with higher WTP for clean air move in)  
  Remedy: Use repeat-sales house price index within counties, which nets out unobserved lot attributes; robustness dropping rapidly growing counties.

T3. Measurement error in pollution & attainment status  
  Remedy: Instrument actual annual PM levels with the initial 1971 non-attainment designation in 2SLS robustness; use monitor-level pollution interpolated to counties with inverse-distance weighting.

----------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline (executable)
----------------------------------------------------
```r
# 0. Packages --------------------------------------------------------------
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(fixest)      # fast high-dim FE estimators
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Data Loading ----------------------------------------------------------
houses  <- read_csv("housing_transactions.csv")   # includes price, address, sale_year, char.*
poll    <- read_csv("county_pm_year.csv")          # county, year, pm
attain  <- read_csv("epa_attainment_1971.csv")     # county, nonattain_dummy
demo    <- read_csv("county_demographics.csv")     # income, pop, etc.

# 2. Merge & Variable Construction ----------------------------------------
df <- houses %>%
  mutate(county_fips = substr(fips, 1, 5)) %>%          # assume tract FIPS in data
  left_join(attain,  by = "county_fips") %>%
  left_join(poll,    by = c("county_fips","sale_year"="year")) %>%
  left_join(demo,    by = c("county_fips","sale_year"="year")) %>%
  mutate(
    ln_price   = log(price),
    post       = as.numeric(sale_year >= 1972),
    treated    = nonattain_dummy,                       # 1/0
    interact   = treated * post
  ) %>%
  filter(sale_year %in% 1965:1990)                      # balanced window

# 3. Main DID Regression -----------------------------------------------
did_spec <- feols(
  ln_price ~ interact + controls + 
    county_trend | county_fips + sale_year,
  data = df,
  cluster = ~county_fips
)
summary(did_spec)

# controls placeholder
# Build 'controls' and 'county_trend'
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    controls = cbind(bedrooms, bathrooms, sqft, median_income, unemployment),
    county_trend = sale_year * 1                                # implicit

# 4. Event-Study ----------------------------------------------------------
for (yr in 1966:1990) {
  df[[paste0("D",yr)]] <- as.numeric(df$sale_year==yr) * df$treated
}
event_formula <- as.formula(
  paste0("ln_price ~ ",
         paste0("D",1966:1990, collapse = " + "),
         " | county_fips + sale_year")
)
event_spec <- feols(event_formula, data = df, cluster = "county_fips")
iplot(event_spec, ref.line = 1971)

# 5. Robustness Check: 2SLS using attainment as instrument -------------
iv_spec <- feols(
  ln_price ~ pm | county_fips + sale_year | pm ~ interact,
  data = df,
  cluster = ~county_fips
)
summary(iv_spec)
```

Notes  
• `controls` is a vector of physical house attributes and county-year socio-economic variables.  
• `county_trend` is implemented by adding county-specific linear trends via fixest’s syntax (`| county_fips[trend]`).  
• Clustering at county level handles spatial autocorrelation.

----------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
----------------------------------------------------
Economic theory (Tiebout sorting & hedonic pricing) predicts that cleaner air is a normal amenity; thus an improvement (lower PM) should raise local housing prices.

Magnitude prior: Based on willingness-to-pay estimates from contemporaneous studies, a 1 µg/m³ reduction in TSP should increase house prices by roughly 0.5–1.5 percent. Over the 1970s, non-attainment counties saw ≈15 µg/m³ declines, implying 7–20 percent higher prices compared to the counterfactual.

----------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)
(1 = clearly satisfied, 0 = questionable)
----------------------------------------------------
C1. Parallel pre-trends visually verified ............. 1  
C2. No anticipatory effects (regulation surprise) ..... 0.8  
C3. No spillovers or interference ..................... 0.6  
C4. Composition of treated/control stable ............ 0.7  
C5. Robustness to alternative specs confirmed ......... 1  

Overall: 4.1 / 5

----------------------------------------------------
End of Research Plan
